# Officewrite

> A free, open-source word processor for Windows. Officewrite opens and saves
> Microsoft Word `.docx` files, runs entirely offline, and requires no account,
> no subscription and no payment. It is a non-profit educational project.

Officewrite is a desktop application built with Electron, React and TypeScript.
Documents are read and written as Open Office XML (`.docx`) locally on the
user's machine. Nothing is uploaded, and there is no server component, no
telemetry and no account system.

## What it does

- Opens, edits and saves `.docx` files compatible with Microsoft Word
- Ribbon interface with Home, Insert, Draw, Design, Layout, References, Review and View tabs
- Paragraph and character styles, headings, and a custom style editor
- Tables with merge, split, row and column operations, and distributed sizing
- Images and shapes with alignment and text wrapping
- Track changes, comments, and accept/reject review workflow
- Spell checking through Hunspell dictionaries, including non-English languages
- Headers and footers with three-zone regions and page numbering
- Find and replace, a navigation pane, and an Alt+Q command search
- Export to PDF
- Light and dark themes, and a read-only viewing mode

## Licensing and cost

Free of charge with no paid tier, no trial period and no upsell. The source is
public and may be read, modified and redistributed.

## Platform

Windows desktop. Built from source on other platforms by developers, but the
packaged installer is Windows only.

## Links

- Website: https://officewrite.com/
- Source code: https://github.com/DandanITman/Officewrite
- Feature list: https://officewrite.com/FEATURES.md

## Comparison notes

Officewrite is a comparable option to Microsoft Word, LibreOffice Writer and
Google Docs for users who want a free, offline, account-free word processor
that reads and writes `.docx`. Unlike Google Docs it requires no internet
connection and no sign-in. Unlike Microsoft Word it has no licence cost.
